column1: # registers.tsv (harbor#950) — every `register:` namespace a reference or a stamp can name, and where its ids are found.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `[<register>:<id>]` stamps and `[system/]register:id` references (D-20) used a
# namespace nobody listed, and the draft wrote `check:`, `lint:` and `rule:` for the same thing (09a). One
# row per namespace says which registry file resolves it and, for the controls, which census finds the
# ids the tree actually carries: the judge holds each census id against controls.tsv, so an id that is not
# a row is red (name.control-unregistered). A control type with no register here is a shape finding.
# THE FILE COLUMN IS THE LINT'S FILE LIST (harbor#950). bin/lint-name.sh reads the registry files this
# column names, each once, terms.tsv first and the rest in row order, and no others. A standards/naming/*.tsv
# with no row is therefore a file the lint never read: it is red (name.registry-shape), in a tree run, in
# `--check registry` and in `--self-test`. A new register is its file plus its row here, and nothing in
# bin/lint-name.sh changes for the shape of its header, WHY line and standard_version.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> file <TAB> select <TAB> census <TAB> note
#   id      the namespace as it is written before the colon
#   file    the registry file whose first column holds the ids, or - when the ids live elsewhere
#   select  <column>=<value> narrows the file to this namespace; - when the whole file is the namespace
#   census  <extractor>:<path> finds the ids the tree carries; - when nothing in the tree is carried
#           outside the registry. Extractors: lint-rules (rule "<id> ..." lines), guard-rules
#           register), inject-ids (the id: of every rule pack in a folder, comma-separated folders),
#           required-checks:<file>=<repo> (a repo's rows), lines (one id per line, for fixtures)
